title: Determine the four-color triangle Ramsey number R(3,3,3,3)
statement: Determine the least positive integer N such that every map from the unordered pairs of {1,...,N} to {1,2,3,4} gives some three distinct vertices whose three pair colors are equal.
source_locator: DS1.18 section 6.1.1, printed page 56 (PDF page index 55); Fettes–Kramer–Radziszowski abstract; Kiem–Pokutta–Spiegel section 2.
status_basis: The April 2026 author-maintained survey explicitly calls this open and states 51 <= N <= 62. Targeted October 2026 searches found no source establishing an exact value; the inspected recent-sounding multiplicity paper addresses a different quantity. This is a scoped literature check, not proof that no solution exists.
plain_summary: How many vertices force a same-colored triangle when every pair is assigned one of four colors? Existing constructive and universal bounds leave a gap.
assumptions: Finite simple complete graph K_N, without loops.
Coloring is a total map from unordered two-element vertex subsets to {1,2,3,4}; not all colors need occur.
A monochromatic triangle uses three distinct vertices with all three pair colors equal.
No restrictions such as cyclicity, group constructions, or balanced color-class sizes are imposed.
scope: The unrestricted finite threshold. A restricted construction class or a single improved bound is valuable partial progress but does not determine the exact number.
target: Find an exact integer N and establish both a triangle-free four-coloring of K_(N-1) and a proof that no such coloring of K_N exists.
success_criteria: For a lower bound, serialize a complete coloring and independently test all vertex triples.
For an upper bound, supply a complete mathematical proof or a complete encoding with a independently checkable unsatisfiability proof and justified symmetry reductions.
For exact determination, the certified lower and upper bounds must coincide.
Document theorem assumptions, source versions, computation artifacts, reviewer scope, and unresolved gaps.
A certified improvement alone is labeled partial progress, not resolution.
known_results: The April 2026 dynamic survey gives 51 <= R(3,3,3,3) <= 62 and explicitly calls the exact value open.
Fettes, Kramer, and Radziszowski establish the upper bound 62 (2004).
The Kiem–Pokutta–Spiegel asymptotic multiplicity theorem concerns triangle density, not this finite threshold.
prerequisites: Extremal graph theory and Ramsey bounds
SAT/constraint programming and certificate checking for computational approaches
Literature on critical colorings and structural upper-bound arguments
significance: A concrete unresolved finite parameter connects extremal constructions, structural graph theory, and computational proof. Its apparent simplicity does not make its search space tractable.

relations.explanation: The two-color known-result case can test encoding and checking, without predicting performance at the open four-color scale.
Both seek finite Ramsey thresholds, but color counts and forbidden clique sizes differ; they are not duplicate or equivalent problems.

requirements.data: Public papers and, for a future attempt, existing lower-bound colorings with checked provenance. No empirical dataset required.
requirements.compute: Unassessed and potentially substantial. The naive space at N vertices is 4^(N*(N-1)/2). Structural restrictions, solver complexity, certificate storage, and checking cost require separate planning. No hardware, runtime, fee, or affordable-solution promise is made.
requirements.theoretical_assumptions: Ordinary finite combinatorics. Every symmetry breaking or restricted construction must have its scope proved. Approximate SDP output is not by itself an upper-bound certificate.
